text: Code refactoring means improving the structure of existing code without changing what it does. The program's behavior stays the same, but the code becomes cleaner and easier to understand. Good refactoring improves readability, so other developers can read and maintain the code more easily. It also helps reduce technical debt, which builds up when quick fixes and messy code are left in place. By refactoring regularly, teams avoid bigger problems later. Refactoring is not about adding new features; it is about making the code simpler, clearer, and easier to work with in the future.
